newsitem.title: BENIN: Benin hikes cost of water, electricity.
newsitem.headline: Benin hikes cost of water, electricity.

text.p: The West African state of Benin has hiked tariffs for water and electricity by up to 40 percent for some consumers, official sources said.
Under new tariffs which came into effect on January 1, domestic users of electricity will pay five percent more, while for industrial consumers the rise is 10 percent.
The water bill for domestic users goes up by 20 percent while industrial consumers pay 40 percent more. Unit costs were not available for either service.

The new rates meant to help improve the finances of cash-strapped Electricity and Water Company of Benin, were to take effect last April but were delayed by former president Nicephore Soglo who faced elections about that time. He lost a bid for a second term.

The company, which buys power from Ghana and Ivory Coast, received a subsidy of three billion CFA francs following a 50 percent devaluation of the regional CFA currency in Januray 1994 but this was halted in 1995.
The company's 1997 provisional deficit is projected at 2.4 billion CFA.
